run.title: Write an I2C driver for BMP180 on STM32F303RE from scratch
run.taskPrompt:
Write an I2C driver for BMP180 on STM32F303RE from scratch.
- I2C1: SDA=PB9, SCL=PB8
- LA wiring: CH0=SDA, CH1=SCL
Goal: verify sensor is working.

plan.title: Inspect existing repo files
plan.detail: Read main.c and Makefile to understand the current skeleton, confirm MCU flags, linker script, and what RTT/SEGGER headers are available.

plan.title: Write BMP180 I2C firmware in main.c
plan.detail: Implement from scratch: (1) RCC enable for GPIOB and I2C1; (2) PB8/PB9 AF4 open-drain config; (3) I2C1 init with TIMINGR=0x10420F13 for 100 kHz SM at 8 MHz HSI; (4) BMP180 chip-id read (reg 0xD0 → expect 0x55); (5) read 22 calibration bytes from 0xAC; (6) trigger uncompensated temperature (0xF4=0x2E) and pressure (0xF4=0x34) measurements; (7) compute true temperature and pressure via BMP180 datasheet algorithm; (8) print results over RTT (SEGGER_RTT_printf). Repeat in a loop every 2 s.

plan.title: Build firmware
plan.detail: Run 'make clean && make' via build_firmware. Confirm exit code 0 and that rtt-f303re.elf is produced.

plan.title: Flash firmware to Nucleo-F303RE
plan.detail: Use pyocd flash --target stm32f303retx rtt-f303re.elf. This is an approval-gated hardware mutation.

plan.title: Capture I2C bus traffic with logic analyzer
plan.detail: Run capture_during (I2C decode on CH0=SDA, CH1=SCL) while the board is running. Verify SCL frequency ~100 kHz, device ACK at 0x77, chip-id byte 0x55 visible in the decode.

plan.title: Read RTT log
plan.detail: Use read_firmware_log to capture RTT output. Confirm 'CHIP_ID=0x55', calibration coefficients printed, and TEMP/PRESS values in physically plausible ranges.

plan.title: Record all checks and write final report
plan.detail: Record pass/fail for every registered check citing artifact IDs. Call write_report with objective, procedure, measurements, and reproduction steps.

payload.riskSummary: Two hardware mutations occur: (1) flash_firmware writes new code to the Nucleo-F303RE's internal flash via pyocd — this is approval-gated and will overwrite whatever was previously programmed; (2) the logic analyzer capture drives no power onto the bus (passive tap) and is low-risk. The board is powered over USB/ST-LINK 3V3; the BMP180 is a 3.3 V device, so no voltage mismatch risk. I2C lines are open-drain with MCU internal pull configuration; external pull-ups on the BMP180 module are assumed. No erase-beyond-flash is required. All other steps (source edit, build, RTT read) are purely software.

lines: I'll analyze the task context carefully before declaring the plan.
**Key facts gathered:**
- STM32F303RE, 8 MHz HSI clock
- I2C1 on PB8 (SCL) / PB9 (SDA), alternate function AF4
- BMP180 at 7-bit address 0x77, chip-id register 0xD0 → expected 0x55
- BMP180 calibration registers at 0xAC–0xBF (11 coefficients), measurement control at 0xF4, result at 0xF6
- LA: CH0=SDA, CH1=SCL (Kingst LA2016)
- RTT log channel only (no UART)
- Existing repo has a bare `main.c` and `Makefile`
**TIMINGR for 100 kHz I2C at 8 MHz HSI:**
Standard-mode at 8 MHz: PRESC=1, SCLL=0x13, SCLH=0x0F, SDADEL=0x2, SCLDEL=0x4 → TIMINGR = 0x10420F13 (from STM32CubeMX reference for 8 MHz / SM 100 kHz)
Plan approved. Starting execution — first, inspect the existing repo files and list connected hardware simultaneously.
